about: Living things found in places. An animal may name the species that represents it in play; a plant may name the item it yields when gathered. Habitats map to Orsino terrains where one exists.

yarrow.name: Yarrow
yarrow.signs: Flat pale flower heads above feathery leaves.
yarrow.stand: Yarrow grows in the grass at the wayside, flat white heads over feathery leaves: a soldier's herb, for cuts.

alder.name: Alder
alder.signs: Dark cone-like catkins and roots at the water line.

red_deer.name: Red deer
red_deer.signs: Split hoofprints and stripped sapling bark.

source.notes: No Kyr game species yet; the deer is scenery that a woodcraft company can approach.

otter.name: Otter
otter.signs: Webbed prints and fish scales on a flat stone.

grey_wolf.name: Grey wolf
grey_wolf.signs: Paired tracks and coarse grey fur on a low branch.

willow.name: Willow
willow.signs: Grey-green leaves, long whippy shoots, and roots in the bank.
willow.stand: Willows lean out over the water here, grey-green, their roots in the bank and their long shoots trailing in the current.

source.notes: Willow bark breaks a fever; the herb-wives of every country know it.

meadowsweet.name: Meadowsweet
meadowsweet.signs: Froth of cream flowers, smelling of almonds.
meadowsweet.stand: Meadowsweet grows thick along the wet ground, a froth of cream flowers that smells of almonds and honey.

source.notes: For pain and the stomach; strewn on floors.

sphagnum.name: Sphagnum moss
sphagnum.signs: Red and green moss in the wet hollows, holding water like a sponge.
sphagnum.stand: Sphagnum moss lies in the wet hollows, red and green, holding water like a sponge: it binds a wound better than linen.

source.notes: Dried and packed into wounds, as field dressings have been.
